classification: local two-point rehearsal of the PITR custody and restore tooling; not off-host, not the public-API application drill, not DR

host.docker: Docker Desktop engine 29.7.2 (Linux VM); commands ran from a Linux helper container

source: working tree on branch ops-5/joint-pitr-recovery from 1df69a25

cli.built_from: debug synveda-cli from this source layered on the pitr image

report.scope: local two-point PITR custody and restore tooling; no gateway, Keycloak or public API
report.repository: local seaweedfs over verified private-CA TLS on an isolated Docker network

rpo.definition: loss window = commits after the last archived WAL segment at the loss instant; archive_timeout bounds it

report.rto_definition: first restore command (custody open) to restored cluster promoted and recovery-verify passed; excludes fetching custody, application start and browser login

rewrap.note: retain the previous KEK with every backup taken before this replacement

kek_replacement.retiring_kek_refused: synveda: recovery verification found tenant key reference local:ops5-drill-2 but the configured KEK is local:ops5-drill-1; supply the custody set that holds it

deterministic.rust: cargo fmt --check; strict clippy -D warnings for synveda-crypto/-audit/-store/-cli all targets
deterministic.rust_linux: Linux container (rust 1.96 bookworm, non-root): synveda-cli bin tests 220/220, synveda-store lib 47 passed and 3 ignored
deterministic.rust_native: Windows host: synveda-crypto 24/24, synveda-audit 39/39; synveda-cli bin and synveda-store lib tests that depend on private-file ACLs and POSIX paths fail natively here and pass in the Linux run above
deterministic.store_database: synveda-store --test keys 15/15 against a fresh PostgreSQL 17.11/pgvector 0.8.7 fixture with ordinary gateway and migrator roles, including tenant rewrap compare-and-set under RLS
deterministic.native_cli: kms rewrap against a fresh fixture: 2 tenant generations rewrapped, idempotent rerun 0, third reference refused, identical reference refused, one tenant.key.rewrapped event; recovery-verify refused the retiring KEK and accepted the replacement
deterministic.compose_gate: Linux container on an exact LF snapshot: the check-compose-contract node suites plus consumer recovery/compose and pitr-recovery tests, including real Compose renders of the pitr-backup, pitr-restore (with and without CA) and kek-rewrap file sets; scripts/check-compose-contract.mjs passes
deterministic.deploy_gates: with pinned Helm v4.2.3: check-release-parity, check-deploy-convergence and their node tests pass on the change and on the clean HEAD baseline
deterministic.sqlx: five new query files generated by cargo sqlx prepare 0.8.6 against a product-migrated portable-lineage database

limits: No gateway, worker, Keycloak, proxy or browser ran; identity state was a stand-in table in the keycloak database of the same cluster

The compose.sh pitr-backup, pitr-mark, pitr-restore and kek-rewrap actions and pitr-drill.sh ran only against fake Docker plus real Compose rendering; the rehearsal drove the same planner, wrapper, CLI and SQL directly
The S3 server was local on an isolated Docker network; nothing left the host
Seconds to verified measure custody open through promotion and recovery-verify on a database of a few megabytes
No owner-approved RPO, RTO, retention or drill cadence exists
hardening: repository and restore one-shots ran with the Compose service's read-only root, cap_drop ALL plus CHOWN/DAC_OVERRIDE/FOWNER/SETGID/SETUID, no-new-privileges, tmpfs /tmp and a runtime-UID-owned 0600 configuration
